subject: hedgehog
title: Hedgehogs Hear 85,000 Hertz, Higher Than Dogs or Cats Can

scenes.text: A hedgehog hears sounds your dog can't.
Your ears stop around twenty thousand hertz. A dog's, around forty-five thousand.
Scientists tested twenty rescued hedgehogs. They heard up to eighty-five thousand, over four times your limit.
Their hearing is sharpest around forty thousand hertz, a pitch you'd never notice.
That could save them. In some places, roads may kill up to one in three hedgehogs.
The idea is cars that beep at a pitch only hedgehogs would hear. You'd never know.

description:
European hedgehogs hear from about 4,000 to 85,000 hertz, with peak sensitivity near 40,000 hertz, beyond the range of humans (about 20,000), dogs (about 45,000) and cats (about 65,000).
Researchers recorded the brain responses of 20 rehabilitated hedgehogs. Since roads may kill up to a third of some local populations, they suggest ultrasonic warning sounds on cars could help.
Have you ever seen a hedgehog in the wild?
first_comment: Cats top out around 65,000 hertz, so the hedgehog beats them too. Would you put a hedgehog beeper on your car?
